Fresh CPU reads and 64-element signed-INT4 quantization of the four frozen layer-0/1 gate/up tensors reproduce every tensor shape/hash, every per-tensor symbol hash and the complete 14,680,064-symbol ledger byte-for-byte.

Independent CPU Huffman decoding of all 114,688 restart blocks reproduces the symbol ledger exactly. Independent nibble unpack of int4_packed.bin is also exact. This verifies physical packing and round trip without a GPU rerun.

Physical sizes independently reproduce 6,478,036 bitstream bytes plus 458,752 offset bytes plus 8,192 lookup bytes = 6,944,980 bytes, or 3.7847137451171875 bits/element. Even excluding all offset and codebook overhead, empirical code lengths require 3.5029142243521556 bits/element, so accounting cannot rescue the frozen 3.0 gate.

The ten bound timing batches reproduce medians 1.3183660888671875 ms Huffman and 0.043356161117553714 ms INT4, input throughput 5.267869113629514 GB/s and penalty 30.407814134942345x. All thresholds are recomputed from retained raw batch values.

Adversarial batch sensitivity remains far from qualification: choosing the fastest Huffman batch yields only 5.342129278844687 GB/s, and pairing fastest Huffman with slowest INT4 still gives 25.67381091817008x. Counting decoded output bytes instead of compressed input would be about 11.14 GB/s, also far below 100 GB/s.

The packed Huffman representation is only 5.382% smaller than physical INT4. The paired service PID and health remain stable and 25 warmups precede five 100-iteration CUDA-event batches; lack of clock/utilization telemetry limits fine attribution but cannot plausibly bridge the 18.7x throughput and 12.8x penalty margins in these stable batches.

The negative is retained only for this frozen 128-symbol restart codec, lookup decoder, four Qwen tensors and RTX 3090 screen. It does not reject entropy coding universally, a different parallel decoder or block size, serving integration, VRAM reduction, model quality or end-to-end latency.
